videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: From Wakefield, West Yorkshire, Michael visits the National Coal Mining Museum for England at Caphouse Colliery. He pauses to admire the tall spire of Wakefield Cathedral and its resident peregrine falcons before heading to the banks of the Calder.

videos.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo continues his 1,000-mile journey from the northern state of Minnesota to the home of the blues in Memphis, Tennessee. At the ornate Palmer House Hotel, Michael recreates the original chocolate Brownie.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
videos.description: Beginning with a look at the early use of wind and water power, Fred traces the development of the steam engine and visits a man who has built a windmill in his own back garden. He then sets off in search of early beam engines that are still functioning today.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
videos.description: Travelling from the Scottish countryside of New Lanark to Burnley, Fred talks to ex weavers about life in the mills and meets a group of volunteers who have spent 30 years saving mill engines.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
videos.description: Fred shifts his attention to the development of the iron and steel industries, starting with Ironbridge Gorge in Shropshire. He comes across a rolling mill which he remembers once operating in Bolton, tries his hand at chain making, and then it's eyes-on-stalks time as Fred drives the biggest steam rolling mill engine he has ever seen.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
videos.description: Starting in Cornwall and travelling all the way to Scotland, Fred turns his eye to the practice of mining. On his travels, he finds out exactly how tin, slate, lead and coal were all extracted from the ground.

videos.title: Saving Lives at Sea
videos.description: In Port Isaac, on the north coast of Cornwall, the crew race to the rescue of a female casualty with a spinal injury. With the light fading, she's in a precarious position on a rock face.

videos.title: Train Rescue Down Under
videos.description: A busy loco maintenance team expects the unexpected, installing a challenging water tank on a vintage loco. An electronics team fights e-waste.

videos.title: Martin Clunes: Islands of America
videos.description: The first port of call on Martin's journey is Hawaii. His exploration looks beyond Hawaii's image as a tourist paradise, crammed with sun-kissed beaches and world-class surfing, and into the havoc wreaked by advancing lava fields and smoking craters.

videos.title: Martin Clunes: Man to Manta
videos.description: Actor Martin Clunes has been a keen surface diver for over ten years and he has a deep fascination for manta rays. Boasting a wingspan of 25 feet, manta rays are one of the most mysterious and gentle giants of the ocean.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: On the last leg of his 300-mile journey across the north and the Midlands, Robbie Cumming faces issues with ice on the Grand Union Canal. He takes on Foxton's famous lock flight in Leicestershire and completes his journey in the picturesque village Braunston, Northamptonshire, regarded as the spiritual home for narrowboaters.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Life on England's waterways with Robbie Cumming. A low canal tunnel in Staffordshire proves a problem, and Robbie helps out a stranded boater.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: The reality of life afloat with Robbie Cumming. A fallen tree and a leaking lock pound hamper Robbie's journey across the Pennines.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: The real side of boat life with Robbie Cumming. Robbie runs aground on the Rochdale Canal - will he make it to Manchester?

videos.title: Bill Bailey's Jungle Hero
videos.description: Comedian Bill Bailey heads to the jungles of Indonesia in the footsteps of his hero, Victorian naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace, to understand how he came up with the theory of evolution independently of Darwin. In the first of this two part series, Bill retraces Wallace's explorations from the jungles of Borneo to the exotic islands of Indonesia, encountering orangutans, flying frogs and extraordinary bugs.

videos.title: The Green Planet
videos.description: Water plants create some of the most beautiful, bizarre and important habitats on earth. To hold on in torrents, plants use a kind of superglue. Some are armed with vicious weapons to fight titanic battles for space. Others form perfect spheres and escape from animal enemies by rolling. Where nutrients are washed away, plants turn into hunters of animals, laying traps and even counting to ensure their success.

videos.title: The Green Planet
videos.description: Between the tropics and the frozen poles lies a region dominated by relentless change in the form of the four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. Each one presents plants with huge challenges, from ice and snow to raging fires, from intense competition to surprising enemies. This is a world of astonishing variety and vibrant colour. To survive here plants must use strategy, deception and remarkable feats of engineering. Most importantly, they must get their timing right.

videos.title: Bangers & Cash: Restoring Classics
videos.description: The team opt for a 1965 Ford Cortina Estate, supposedly owned by a South African Chief of Police, and take on one of Dave's guilty pleasures: a 1980s Austin Morris Max.

videos.title: Bangers & Cash: Restoring Classics
videos.description: It's a battle of little and large as the team get creative with a 1996 Fiat 126 and then run their own consumer test on a 2004 Bentley Continental GT.

videos.title: Inside Bentley: A Great British Motor Car
videos.description: Bentley Motors have been building bespoke cars for the rich and famous for almost a century, and for the first time in their long history, the doors of its historic home in northwest England have been opened to the cameras.

videos.title: Yes, Minister
videos.description: Jim talks up his involvement in a public-private partnership project, not knowing the financial irregularities that could lead to land him in hot water. The only way out seems to give a part-time government appointment that he is trying to abolish.

videos.title: Yes, Minister
videos.description: The Minister sees an opportunity to further his career when a newly built and fully staffed hospital seems to have no patients.

videos.title: Yes, Minister
videos.description: Jim Hacker plans to block honours for civil servants until cost-cutting measures are introduced in their departments. Naturally, Sir Humphrey plans his own retaliation.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Paul picks up a stunning 1961 Vauxhall Cresta, Dave drools over a Ford Sierra Sapphire Cosworth, and Derek refuses a test drive in the world's smallest production car, the 3.5 horsepower Peel P50.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Derek inspects a collection of old police cars that includes a Rover P6 complete with radio, sirens and V8 engine. Meanwhile, Paul tries to figure out who will buy an old 1975 Range Rover that has been converted into a fire engine.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo heads for leafy Hatch End, where he investigates an illustrator whose work was so popular in the 1920s and 30s that his name entered the English dictionary. William Heath Robinson's great-nephew talks Michael through some of the mad contraptions the artist used to satirise technology.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: From Wakefield, West Yorkshire, Michael visits the National Coal Mining Museum for England at Caphouse Colliery. He pauses to admire the tall spire of Wakefield Cathedral and its resident peregrine falcons before heading to the banks of the Calder.

videos.title: Teleshopping
videos.description: Presenting the latest products live on television that can be ordered directly. The product range extends from vacuum cleaners and bath towels to sports equipment.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo resumes his tour of the Home Counties in the picturesque and historic county town of Guildford. His 1936 Bradshaw's guide commends its 'fine old castle keep' and guildhall but makes no mention of its hilltop cathedral. Michael meets head guide Janet Matthews to discover the origins of the first Anglican cathedral to be built on a new site in the south of England since the Reformation, begun in 1936.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo continues his post-war exploration of North West England in Bradford, Shipley and Hebden Bridge. In Centenary Square in Bradford, Michael encounters the literary giant JB Priestley, author of `An Inspector Calls'.

videos.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
videos.description: Michael stops at rural Mattoon, where he gets a taste of the tough early life, which shaped President Abraham Lincoln. Wiping the sweat from his brow, Michael struggles to split one rail compared with Lincoln's estimated 700-a-day.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
videos.description: Fred's fascinating journey through Britain's industrial past sees him tracing the development of the railways, from the first steam locomotive to the record-breaking Mallard. The excitement reminds him of his childhood days when locomotives used to roar past his bedroom window, and Fred gets his hands dirty stoking the boiler of a Black Five as he speeds through the Welsh countryside.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
videos.description: Fred moves on to the golden age of shipbuilding, examining the skills of engineers who turned Britain into one of the foremost manufacturing nations. He also visits the world's first production line in Suffolk.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Age of Steam
videos.description: Part 1/6. Fred visits Cornwall to explore its key place in the early history of the steam engine. In Cornwall, Fred illustrates how the county's tin mining industry utilised steam engines to pump water.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Age of Steam
videos.description: Part 2/6. Fred Dibnah explores the revolutionary impact of steam engines on rail transport. In the process, Fred examines both the earliest colliery railways and the end of steam power on commercial railways in the 1960s.

videos.title: Martin Clunes: Islands of America
videos.description: Martin's travels take him 1,500 miles to the San Juan Islands in Washington State, just off America's North West Pacific coast, right on the border with Canada. There are more than 100 islands, mostly uninhabited. From the San Juan Islands, Martin travels down America's West coast to visit the Channel Islands National Park, which is known as `America's Galapagos' because of its unique wildlife. From the Channel Islands, Martin takes a 2,000-mile journey across the States to Louisiana.

videos.title: Martin Clunes: Man to Manta
videos.description: Actor Martin Clunes has been a keen surface diver for over ten years and he has a deep fascination for manta rays. Boasting a wingspan of 25 feet, manta rays are one of the most mysterious and gentle giants of the ocean.

videos.title: David Jason's Great British Inventions
videos.description: Sir David finds out about the invention of the incandescent light bulb, the world's first lawnmower and the development of the telephone, as he learns about the British innovations that have transformed our homes.

videos.title: David Jason's Secret Service
videos.description: Passionate espionage enthusiast Sir David Jason searches for the origins of the British Secret Service and discovers the legendary characters, audacious missions and makeshift methods that characterised the early days of spying.

videos.title: Operation Arctic with Simon Reeve
videos.description: Gordon meets the Polar Bear Cops tasked with keeping the town safe. Kate heads to Sweden to help round up some reindeer and Simon joins the intrepid NASA scientists monitoring the melt of Greenland's glaciers. Plus, all the live action from the bears out on the tundra.

videos.title: Operation Arctic with Simon Reeve
videos.description: Kate meets the Inuit artists inspired by the changing world around them, while Simon heads off on a fishing expedition, Arctic style. In Churchill, Gordon finds out how the town deals with their more troublesome bears when he follows the eviction of a repeat offender.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: On the last leg of his journey across England, Robbie crosses an epic aqueduct near Stratford-upon-Avon and gets stuck in a lock in central Birmingham.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Narrowboater Robbie Cumming begins his 170-mile journey across the north of England and soon runs into difficulty when he encounters a propeller problem in Wigan and runs aground in Blackburn. Nevertheless, he pushes on to navigate a true wonder of the waterways, the Burnley Embankment.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Narrowboater and film-maker Robbie Cumming crosses the Pennines on the picturesque Leeds and Liverpool Canal, and lends a hand to hire boaters in Gargrave, North Yorkshire. He also encounters Bingley Five Rise Locks, a wonder of the inland waterways.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Jump on board with narrowboater Robbie Cumming as he explores the Victorian village of Saltaire on the Leeds and Liverpool Canal, moors up in Leeds and goes in search of an abandoned waterway on the Aire and Calder Navigation.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Fallen trees block Robbie's journey on the Peak Forest Canal. Later, he meets TV host Terry Christian, whose dad once worked a local waterway.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Robbie struggles with grounding out, a tangled prop and constant challenges on the Rochdale Canal - known as the 'Everest of Canals' - to reach its highest point.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: There is a triple collection of desirable cars in store for Derek when an MG Midget, an Austin-Healey frogeye Sprite and an RS2000 come up for auction.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Paul sets out for County Durham in order to collect both a 1936 Singer Le Mans sports car and a pristine 1957 Lambretta LD 150. In the meantime, Derek gets his hands on a 1962 MGA MK2 Coupe.

videos.description: Michael is heading for Farnborough, Hampshire, famous today for its air show and home to what was then the Royal Aircraft Establishment. Richard Gardner of the Farnborough Air Sciences Trust tells Michael about the boffins who worked here and the inventions they came up with, such as retractable landing gear and flight-pressurised suits.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo travels through the Britain of his youth from London's Docklands and East End to the 'city within a city', the Barbican. At Tilbury, he traces the arrival in 1948 of the Empire Windrush.

videos.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
videos.description: Beginning in the Silver State of Nevada, Michael takes to the skies over the dramatic Sierra Nevada mountain range. At Lake Tahoe, he hears of the first European explorer, known as 'The Pathfinder', whose discovery opened up the west for settlement. Travelling on the historic Virginia and Truckee heritage line, Michael investigates the vast deposits of silver and gold ore on which Virginia City was built.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Paul and Charlie have the rare chance to pick up a trio of difficult-to-tame, classic British vehicles, iconic Austin-Healeys in varying conditions.

videos.title: Bangers & Cash: Restoring Classics
videos.description: The team head for restoration in their Bedford Rascal Camper van. They also purchase a true British classic - a TR6 - which is almost too good to touch!

videos.title: The World at War
videos.description: Life on the British Home Front is a time of gas masks, digging for victory, evacuation and the Squander Bug. The Luftwaffe redirect their bombing raids to provincial cities and U-boat operations in the Atlantic mean that food supplies are scarce.

videos.title: War Factories
videos.description: The story of the machine gun's development and how it transformed the nature of war. Developed by Hiram Maxim, the world's first fully automatic machine gun weighed 136lbs until British company Vickers adapted the design.

videos.title: Antiques Roadshow
videos.description: The visitors to Castle Ward produce an eclectic mix of finds. Irish treasures include a bronze sculpture known as The Leprechaun, a large table traditionally used for displaying the coffin at a wake and a picture of a fireman in action, brought along by Northern Ireland's first female fire fighter. Treasures from further afield include a Tongan war club that narrowly escaped being chopped up for firewood and a 1960s TV set inspired by the first moon landing.

videos.title: Antiques Roadshow
videos.description: Fiona Bruce discovers what was really inside a 200-year-old bottle of wine that Andy McConnell foolishly tasted in 2016 and traces the history of a chocolate treat in the shape of the nurse that dates back to the First World War.
